extracted.intended_audience: State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Registration Agencies, program sponsors, participating employers, and other apprenticeship stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory requirements for registering and administering (including CTE) registered apprenticeship programs, State Apprenticeship Plan contents, SAA recognition, reporting, data/quality metrics, and related administrative processes. Applies to SAAs, Registration Agencies, program sponsors, and participating employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-compete provisions in CTE agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsor, or a participating employer in the sponsor's program, cannot include in the CTE apprenticeship agreement or otherwise impose on CTE apprentices a non-compete provision or other provision that restricts an apprentice's labor market mobility, including a provision restricting the apprentice's ability to seek or accept employment with another employer prior to the completion of the registered CTE apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on any clause that restricts labor market mobility prior to program completion; applies to sponsors and participating employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on non-disclosure provisions for CTE apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsor, or a participating employer in the sponsor's program, cannot include in the CTE apprenticeship agreement or otherwise impose on CTE apprentices a non-disclosure provision that prevents the worker from working in the same field after the conclusion of the worker's employment with the employer, or that restricts an apprentice's ability to file a complaint with a Registration Agency or other governmental body concerning possible violations of this part or of part 30 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors may include non-disclosure provisions only when they relate to protection of confidential commercial information or trade secrets; cannot be used to bar future employment in the same field or to block complaint filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of executed CTE apprenticeship agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The program sponsor must submit a completed copy of the executed CTE apprenticeship agreement for each CTE apprentice registered to the program's Registration Agency within 30 days of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission requirement to the Registration Agency in a format prescribed by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of completion for registered CTE apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: CTE apprentices who are enrolled in the registered CTE apprenticeship program and who are successful in meeting the CTE apprenticeship-related instruction and the on-the-job training outlined in the industry skills framework will receive a certificate of completion of registered CTE apprenticeship from the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate issuance tied to meeting both related instruction and OJT as outlined in the industry skills framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency application review timeline (CTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency must review an application submitted by a sponsor consistent with paragraph (d)(2) of this section and provide a determination on whether the program is eligible for program registration within 90 days of receipt of a complete application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 90-day decision clock from receipt of a complete application; applies to CTE apprenticeship program registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of registration decisions and denials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency will inform applicants in writing of all decisions regarding program registration. If the Registration Agency denies the application, it must explain in writing the reasons for the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All registration determinations must be communicated in writing; denials require documented reasons to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency outreach and technical assistance responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency is responsible for providing outreach, technical assistance, and any other services to potential sponsors, participating employers, and other potential partners to support the adoption of registered CTE apprenticeship as well as to ensure compliance with the requirements of this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive support role—Registration Agency must provide services to support adoption and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of complaint investigation and anti-retaliation provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint investigation and anti-retaliation provisions in § 29.17 apply to this subpart, except that a Registration Agency may refer complaints under this subsection to the State CTE Agency as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard complaint/anti-retaliation framework applies; Registration Agency may coordinate or refer to State CTE Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review procedures and coordination (CTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: For program reviews under this subpart, the process described in § 29.19 applies. Program reviews should be done in coordination with the relevant State CTE Agency pursuant to the written agreement described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section. The result of any program review will not impact an entity's eligibility for funding under the Perkins program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use § 29.19 procedures; coordinate with State CTE Agency; program reviews do not affect Perkins funding eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration, hearings, and reinstatement processes apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The deregistration process described in § 29.20, the hearing process in § 29.21, and the reinstatement process in § 29.22 will apply to this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard deregistration/hearing/reinstatement procedural provisions used for CTE programs as referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Registration Agencies for CTE apprenticeship — OA fallback
rubrics_metrics.description: OA may serve as the Registration Agency within States where the Administrator has not recognized an SAA to register CTE apprenticeship programs, provided a written agreement has been signed between OA and the State's respective State CTE Agency as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Apprenticeship can act as Registration Agency in absence of recognized SAA, but requires written agreement with State CTE Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition criteria for SAAs to register CTE apprenticeship programs
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs recognized or seeking recognition as a Registration Agency under subpart C will be recognized to register CTE apprenticeship programs provided: (A) The State's proposed or current apprenticeship laws for CTE apprenticeship meet or exceed the requirements for protecting the safety and welfare of CTE apprentices set forth in this subpart; (B) A written agreement has been signed between the SAA and the State CTE Agency; (C) The State has submitted its relevant apprenticeship laws and CTE engagement strategies as described in its State Apprenticeship Plan submission or modification; and (D) The Administrator has approved the State Apprenticeship Plan for both recognition as an SAA and for recognition to register CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four criteria (laws, written agreement, plan submission including CTE strategies, Administrator approval) must be satisfied for SAA recognition as a Registration Agency for CTE.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprentice information reporting within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 calendar days of the start of a CTE apprentice's term, the program sponsor must submit to its Registration Agency in a format prescribed by the Administrator: (1) individual apprentice record level information (including FERPA considerations) such as demographic information, education level, and veteran status; (2) the industry skills framework and occupation; (3) the beginning date and term (duration) of the registered CTE apprenticeship program and the graduated schedule of wages; and (4) any additional CTE apprentice-related information the Administrator considers appropriate or necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of specified individual-level and program placement data in Administrator-prescribed format; must comply with applicable federal privacy laws (e.g., FERPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-semester apprentice status reporting (CTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of each academic semester, the program sponsor must report changes in a CTE apprentice's status to its Registration Agency in a manner prescribed by the Administrator regarding: (1) change in registered CTE apprenticeship status (completion or cancellation); (2) credentials attained during participation; (3) change in employment or education status after participation; (4) wage progression during participation; (5) supportive services provided; and (6) any additional outcomes or services information the Administrator considers appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic (semester) updates on outcomes and services; use prescribed format and include specified outcome fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program sponsor information reporting requirements (CTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the change in status and no less than on an annual basis, for each registered CTE apprenticeship program and industry skills framework, a program sponsor must report to the Registration Agency: (1) up-to-date contact information for each employer participating and collective bargaining signatories if applicable; (2) up-to-date copies of any agreements the sponsor has with each employer and with each CTE apprentice; (3) information about which participating employers have canceled participation; (4) up-to-date information about the program's coordination with credentialing agencies; (5) up-to-date contact information for those designated to receive/process complaints; (6) all unreimbursed costs to the CTE apprentice; and (7) any additional sponsor- or program-level information the Administrator considers appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both change-triggered (within 30 days) and annual reporting obligations for sponsor-level data; prescribed format by Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual quality metrics calculated by Registration Agency (CTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: On an annual basis, for each registered CTE apprenticeship program and industry skills framework, the following quality metrics will be calculated: (1) total number of new and active CTE apprentices annually; (2) total number who successfully completed the sponsor's program annually; (3) annual completion rate; (4) cohort completion rate (cohort definition described); (5) placement rate of exiters in registered apprenticeship programs, postsecondary educational programs, or employment at time of program completion; (6) percentage of exiters receiving at least one recognized postsecondary credential at time of exit; (7) wage at exit; and (8) any additional sponsor- or program-level information the Administrator considers appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency computes these standardized program-level metrics annually in Administrator-prescribed format; cohort completion must compare starters to completers within a designated cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of CTE program and outcome information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator will make on an annual basis general information relating to registered CTE apprenticeship programs along with the information described above publicly available. Upon request of the sponsor, the Administrator may decide not to make the information publicly available for good cause. Additionally, the Administrator will make publicly available a national summary report of CTE apprentices and their outcomes, disaggregated by race, ethnicity, sex, disability status, and other categories determined by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual public reporting requirement with ability to withhold specific sponsor data for good cause upon sponsor request; national summary must be disaggregated by key demographic categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental national/state-level metrics for CTE
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to program metrics, Registration Agencies must use supplemental sources (e.g., wage records, surveys) to calculate at a national or State level at least: (1) placement and retention rate in postsecondary educational programs, registered apprenticeship programs, or employment calculated 6 and 12 months after program completion; (2) annualized average and median earnings of former apprentices calculated over the 6-month period after completion; and (3) percentage of completers who, at 1 year after completion, are earning self-supporting income or have been placed in postsecondary education or a career pathway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supplemental data sources to track medium-term outcomes (6 months, 1 year) and earnings; standardized definitions for placement/retention/earnings expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator evaluations and longitudinal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may conduct evaluations and longitudinal studies to assess the impact and improve the effectiveness of registered CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits Department-led research to evaluate program effectiveness and inform improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency discretion to withhold publication for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency may decide to withhold from publication certain information for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of some data may be restricted when justified by good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor reporting must follow Registration Agency-prescribed manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must report the information described (CTE apprentice and sponsor info) in a manner prescribed by the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format, timing, and submission mechanism determined by Registration Agency per Administrator guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA collection and reporting responsibilities for CTE
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs with an approved State Apprenticeship Plan to serve as a Registration Agency for CTE apprenticeship are required to collect the information from sponsors described above; no less frequently than quarterly SAAs must report the information collected from sponsors; on an annual basis the SAA will report to the Administrator; SAAs may use Department-provided case management system or maintain a State system capable of prescribed reporting and meeting minimum security requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly and annual reporting cadence for SAAs; options for systems to meet reporting/security requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption requests procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for exemption from any provision of this subpart must be made in writing to the Administrator and must contain a statement of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal written request with rationale required for exemptions; submitted to Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice information reporting for general registered apprenticeship (30-day)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 calendar days of the start of an apprentice's participation in a registered apprenticeship program, the program sponsor must submit to its Registration Agency: (i) individual apprentice level information including demographic information, education level, and veteran status; (ii) receipt of pre-apprenticeship services prior to participation, if applicable; (iii) the occupation in which the apprentice is to be trained; (iv) the date the individual became an apprentice; (v) the beginning date and term (duration) of the apprenticeship, the date of the beginning of on-the-job training, the full graduated schedule of wages including the journeyworker wage, and the approximate time to be spent in each work process in the occupation; and (vi) any additional apprentice-related information required by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive individual-level and program placement data required within 30 days for all registered apprentices (not just CTE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice change-of-status reporting (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 calendar days of a change in an apprentice's status, the program sponsor must submit: (i) change in apprenticeship status (completion, transfer, suspension, or cancellation); (ii) interim credentials attained; (iii) employment status; (iv) wage progression; (v) supportive services provided; and (vi) any additional apprentice outcomes or services information required by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely updates required for key status changes and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program sponsor reporting and annual quality metrics (general apprenticeship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the change in status, for each registered apprenticeship program and occupation, a program sponsor must report: (i) up-to-date contact information for the program sponsor; (ii) contact information for each participating employer and collective bargaining signatories if applicable; (iii) up-to-date copy of the program standards adoption agreement with each participating employer; (iv) information about participating employers who canceled; (v) up-to-date information about coordination with credentialing agencies; (vi) contact information for designated complaint recipients; (vii) all unreimbursed costs to the apprentice; and (viii) any additional sponsor or program level information required by the Administrator. On an annual basis the Registration Agency will calculate quality metrics including: (i) total number of apprentices served annually; (ii) total number who successfully completed annually; (iii) annual completion rate; (iv) cohort completion rate; (v) median length of time for program completion; (vi) employment retention rate at time of exit; (vii) percentage of exiters that receive at least one interim credential at time of exit; (viii) percentage of exiters that enter postsecondary education or a career pathway program at time of exit; (ix) apprentice wage at time of exit; (x) information relating to any pre-apprenticeship partnerships; and (xi) any additional sponsor/program level information required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors CTE reporting but applies to all registered apprenticeship programs; includes additional metrics like median time to completion and retention at exit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting and supplemental Registration Agency metrics (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency will make publicly available annual general information relating to registered apprenticeship programs along with the annual metrics. The Agency will make an annual State or national summary report of apprentices and outcomes disaggregated by race, ethnicity, sex, disability status, and other categories. Supplemental calculations must include (i) post-apprenticeship employment retention rate at 6 and 12 months after exit; (ii) annualized average and median earnings over 6 months after completion; (iii) percentage of completers at 1 year after completion who are earning self-supporting income or placed in postsecondary or career pathway; and (iv) Registration Agency metrics including median time for registration, number of programs approved and denied registration, and post-registration customer satisfaction ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive public reporting requirements including medium-term outcomes, earnings, and Registration Agency performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency may withhold publication for good cause (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency may decide to withhold from publication certain information for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same withholding authority as in CTE context; protects certain data when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA roles and responsibilities (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: An SAA is authorized to: (1) implement apprenticeship-related laws and policies approved by Administrator; (2) review, approve, disapprove, and amend standards of apprenticeship and register programs within 90 days of a complete submission for Federal purposes in the State; (3) prescribe apprenticeship agreement content and register apprentices; (4) provide technical assistance to sponsors, employers, apprentices, intermediaries, and stakeholders; (5) collect and report apprenticeship-related data to OA; (6) conduct program reviews of approved programs; (7) establish policies/procedures to promote EEO consistent with part 30; (8) establish basic standards/criteria/requirements for program registration and provide for suspension/deregistration; (9) establish process for registration, suspension, or cancellation of apprenticeship agreements; (10) investigate complaints filed under this part or part 30; and (11) function as a Registration Agency for registered CTE apprenticeship programs pursuant to § 29.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of SAA authorities and duties for Federal purposes; includes 90-day timeline for registration decisions for program submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondelegable duties of SAAs
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for recognition or to maintain recognition, a State cannot delegate, assign, devolve, or relinquish any of the functions that are the responsibility of the SAA under paragraph (a), including intake, evaluation, approval, registration, monitoring, oversight, suspension, or deregistration of apprenticeship programs and standards of apprenticeship within that State, to any external third-party entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core SAA functions must be retained by the SAA and may not be outsourced to external third parties, including State Apprenticeship Councils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish State Apprenticeship Councils and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: An SAA is required to establish and maintain a State Apprenticeship Council operating under the direction of the SAA. The Council may provide written, nonbinding advice, recommendations, research, and reports concerning apprenticeship-related matters. Members must be familiar with occupations suitable for registered apprenticeship, fairly balanced and inclusive of underserved communities, with an equal number of (i) employers or employer representatives, (ii) labor organization or joint labor-management representatives, and (iii) other public members including at least one workforce development system representative and one secondary or postsecondary education representative familiar with registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council is advisory only; membership balance and inclusion of specified roles are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on State Apprenticeship Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Apprenticeship Council is ineligible for recognition as an SAA under this part and is prohibited from assuming or discharging the SAA functions described in paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council cannot perform or be recognized to perform SAA statutory/regulatory functions; it is strictly advisory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity of registration process and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: An SAA must establish a process for providing approval to apprentices, apprenticeship programs, and standards of apprenticeship that are registered in other States by OA or by an SAA for Federal purposes. The process must provide a timely response to a request for reciprocity no later than 45 days after receipt of a program sponsor's application for reciprocity. The reciprocity process must: (1) ensure the program sponsor meets statutory and regulatory wage and hour requirements and apprentice-to-journeyworker ratios of the State where reciprocal approval is sought; (2) ensure the program and individual apprentices who will work in the State are properly registered with the SAA; and (3) ensure the program sponsor develops standards that prepare apprentices to meet or exceed minimum requirements of State or local occupation licensure, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 45-day reciprocity decision timeline; must check statutory wage/hour and ratio compliance and registration and licensure alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for State Apprenticeship Plan submissions and recognition periods
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain recognition or renewal as an SAA, a State must submit a State Apprenticeship Plan beginning December 31, 2026. Recognition (full or provisional) is granted for 4 years from approval. Plans must be submitted at least 120 days prior to the date when seeking recognition. States recognized prior to the effective date must submit a plan by September 1, 2026 to be considered for recognition after December 31, 2026. Subsequent submissions are for 4-year periods beginning July 1, 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific calendar deadlines and recognition period lengths; plans must be timely to maintain recognition continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to approved State Apprenticeship Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved State Apprenticeship Plan requires modification and resubmission when: (A) changes in Federal or State law/policy substantially affect SAA roles; (B) proposed State laws may affect SAA compliance; (C) significant changes in strategies/goals/priorities; or (D) significant changes in statewide vision, strategies, procedures, or organizational structure. Modifications may also be requested by the SAA for other reasons (e.g., change from provisional to full approval, seek recognition as a Registration Agency for CTE). Modifications must be submitted at least 120 days prior to the requested effective date. Modified plans remain approved until the end of the original cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers for mandatory resubmission and flexibility for voluntary modifications; 120-day lead time required for effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the State Apprenticeship Plan — apprenticeship laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The State's proposed or current apprenticeship laws included in the Plan must: (i) allow registration for Federal purposes only for occupations determined suitable pursuant to § 29.7; and (ii) meet or exceed the requirements for protecting safety and welfare of apprentices as set forth in numerous regulatory provisions (§ 29.8, § 29.9, § 29.10, § 29.11, § 29.12, § 29.16, § 29.17, § 29.18, §§ 29.19-29.22, § 29.26, § 29.28, and part 30 EEO requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State laws must align with and meet or exceed federal regulatory standards enumerated in the Plan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required strategic planning elements in State Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan must include: (i) goals for expansion — narrative of State strategic vision/strategy for expanding registered apprenticeship programs including goals/metrics; (ii) strategies for promoting registered apprenticeship programs for underserved communities — narrative including current participant demographics and goals/milestones to track progress; and (iii) aligning education and workforce development activities — narrative describing coordination with WIOA, State Workforce Agency, workforce development board, education entities (higher ed, LEAs, CTE agencies), economic development entities, and intermediaries; and describe efforts to align apprenticeship-related data with education and workforce data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must present measurable goals and narratives describing how apprenticeship expansion, equity, and cross-system alignment will be operationalized and tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required operational planning elements in State Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: States must submit: (i) State EEO plan describing how SAA will promote EEO consistent with part 30; (ii) technical assistance strategies for the plan period; (iii) data reporting processes for meeting quarterly and annual requirements (how SAA will collect and report records); (iv) plan for conducting program reviews; (v) description of how SAA will operationalize registration standards, temporary suspension, cancellation, or deregistration; (vi) reciprocity operationalization; and (vii) description of State Apprenticeship Council structure consistent with § 29.26(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational detail required on EEO, TA, data/reporting, program reviews, registration policies, reciprocity, and council structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances required in State Apprenticeship Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must provide assurances and applicable citations that: (i) the State will provide a process for local registration of National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards recognized by Administrator pursuant to § 29.15; (ii) the State has sufficient resources to carry out SAA functions (outreach, registration, technical assistance, monitoring); (iii) the State will make available on a public website descriptions of laws, policies, and procedures relating to registration and assessment of apprenticeship programs including any additional State requirements and approved State Plans; and (iv) the State requires written assurance from any sponsors registered by the State that they comply with the Support for Veterans in Effective Apprenticeships Act of 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must include concrete assurances about registration processes, resources, transparency, and sponsor compliance with veterans' support law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional plan elements for SAA recognition to serve as Registration Agency for CTE
rubrics_metrics.description: An SAA seeking recognition to serve as a Registration Agency for registered CTE apprenticeship must submit: (i) the State's proposed or current registered CTE apprenticeship laws; (ii) a written agreement between the State entity seeking recognition and the State's CTE Agency; and (iii) a narrative summary of the State's strategic vision and strategy for expanding registered CTE apprenticeship programs under subpart B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional CTE-specific legal, interagency agreement, and strategic narrative elements required for optional CTE Registration Agency recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition designations and criteria (full, provisional, denial)
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, OA will convey one of three designations: (1) Full recognition if State's apprenticeship laws meet/exceed minimum standards; Plan includes all strategic and operational elements responsive to requirements; Plan includes required assurances. (2) Provisional recognition if laws meet minimum standards and assurances are included, but strategic or operational elements are incomplete or nonresponsive, and deficiencies are resolvable with OA technical assistance and an approved corrective action plan (provisional recognition limited to one full planning cycle). (3) Denial of recognition if State laws do not meet minimum standards or SAA unable to be fully approved within one full planning cycle after provisional recognition. Processes for denial/derecognition described in § 29.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-tiered recognition system with corrective-action pathway for provisional recognition and explicit denial criteria; corrective action plans and OA technical assistance may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of OA registration authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding approval of a State Apprenticeship Plan, the Administrator will retain the authority to register apprenticeship programs and apprentices on both a local and nationwide basis for Federal purposes in any State when the Administrator determines that a sponsor seeking registration has satisfied the requirements for registration and such action would further the interests of the National Apprenticeship System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA retains fallback registration authority even when a State is recognized, to be used when it furthers national interests or when sponsor meets requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic monitoring and review of SAAs by OA
rubrics_metrics.description: OA will monitor and review the compliance of an SAA to ensure that it is operating consistent with its approved State Apprenticeship Plan, in instances where the Administrator determines such a review is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA oversight includes periodic compliance checks; triggers for reviews determined by Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derecognition of SAA for noncompliance with approved Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may derecognize an SAA with full or provisional recognition when the Administrator determines that the SAA is not operating consistent with its approved State Apprenticeship Plan. Processes and procedures for such derecognition are described in § 29.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derecognition authority exists for failure to operate per approved Plan; formal procedures govern such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of provisionally approved SAA for failure to submit corrective action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may suspend the authority of a provisionally approved SAA to register new apprenticeship programs for failure to submit, and receive OA's approval of, a corrective action plan as required in paragraph (c)(2). The Administrator will provide written notice to the provisionally approved SAA of the suspension, which will take effect 30 calendar days after the date of the written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisionally recognized SAAs must submit approved corrective action plans when required or face suspension of registration authority after written notice and 30-day effective period.
